_: The Meshes tab after the 2026-08-20 tag-block work: the vocabulary narrows by typing, Enter takes the one match, and a batch labels itself — Shift+Y abandons it. Most steps are judgement calls on purpose — the objective ones are the two that ask whether a token actually landed.

steps.label: look at the tag block before touching it
steps.goal: the block draws the project's whole vocabulary — 55 chips on the furniture kit — so an author reads it rather than remembering it. That is the trade being tested: recognition, at the price of a wall
do: pick any mesh so the detail pane fills
say whether the four axes read as four groups, or as one field of grey boxes
steps.recovery: there is nothing to get wrong — 'it reads as a wall' is the useful answer, not the wrong one

steps.label: find the filter without being told where it is
steps.goal: the box sits between `mount` and `KIND`, and it is the block's first keyboard path. If it has to be pointed out, it is in the wrong place
do: without pressing anything, say where you would type to narrow the chips
then hold K and see where the / badge lands
steps.recovery: if you looked at the list panel's filter box on the right instead, say so — the two say different things on purpose and that is exactly what is being checked

steps.label: narrow it to one token
steps.goal: typing removes chips and never moves the ones that stay. Sears & Shneiderman 1994 measured users slower on menus whose items reordered themselves, which is why this narrows rather than promotes
do: watch the count line under the box, and the three axes that go to `-`
steps.recovery: if the box still shows `filter tags` while you are typing into it, stop and say so — that was a live bug on 2026-08-20 and its fix is what this step is walking

steps.label: take it with Enter
steps.goal: one keystroke does what only a mouse could do before. The block was 55 click targets and nothing else
do: look at where `wood` now sits in LOOKS, and at the status line
steps.recovery: if Enter did nothing, read the count line: more than one token matched, and it refuses rather than guessing. Keep typing until it says `Enter takes it`

steps.label: type the next one without leaving the box
steps.goal: Enter clears the box and keeps the keyboard, so two tokens are one gesture rather than two round trips. Esc is the way out
do: then press Esc and confirm the whole vocabulary is back
steps.recovery: if you had to press / again between the two, say so — that is the loop this step exists to measure

steps.label: which of these did a model decide
steps.goal: since 2026-08-20 a held chip a model wrote and nobody confirmed is pale blue; one you decided is white. The record is per axis, because keeping the model's kind and rewriting its description is the normal case
do: pick a mesh you have labelled with L or Shift+L
say which axes are still the model's guess, reading only the colours
steps.recovery: if every chip is white, this piece has no record yet — that is what every piece labelled before today looks like, and it is deliberately not read as 'a human decided this'

steps.label: watch a batch label itself
steps.goal: since 2026-08-20 a label applies the moment it arrives — no key answers it. The only prompt left is Shift+L when the scope already holds labelled pieces, and approving that runs the lot
do: press Shift+L and read the question if one appears
watch the rows turn green on their own, with your hands off the keyboard
say whether anything landed that you would have rejected
steps.recovery: Shift+Y abandons a walk outright; Cmd+Z undoes one piece. If you wanted a chance to refuse before it was written, that is the finding — say so
